channel.title: The Eternal Argument
channel.description: From Myth to Machine — The Story of Human Thought. A podcast that tells the story of human thought from its earliest beginnings to the present day. Each episode is a story about people wrestling with the hardest questions: What is real? What is good? What are we?
channel.itunes:author: The Eternal Argument
channel.itunes:summary: From Myth to Machine — The Story of Human Thought. A podcast that tells the story of human thought from its earliest beginnings to the present day. Each episode is a story about people wrestling with the hardest questions: What is real? What is good? What are we?

item.title: Ep 1: The Pre-Socratics: Thales to Parmenides
item.description: Water, Fire, and Flux — Ancient Greece (Ionia & Italy). A time of fragmented city-states where thinkers began stripping away the gods to find the "Stuff" (Arche) of the universe.
item.itunes:author: The Eternal Argument

item.title: Ep 2: The Sophists & Socrates
item.description: The Invention of Ethics — The Golden Age of Athens. Democracy is rising, but so is relativism. The Sophists teach how to win arguments; Socrates asks what is true.
item.itunes:author: The Eternal Argument

item.title: Ep 3: Plato I: The Forms
item.description: The Theory of Forms & The Cave — Post-Socrates Athens. Plato tries to stabilize a crumbling world by positing a perfect, eternal realm beyond our senses.
item.itunes:author: The Eternal Argument

item.title: Ep 4: Plato II: The Republic
item.description: Politics & The Soul — The failure of Athenian democracy (which killed Socrates). Plato designs a utopia ruled by philosopher-kings.
item.itunes:author: The Eternal Argument

item.title: Ep 5: Aristotle I: The Toolset
item.description: Metaphysics & Logic — The Macedonian Empire rises. Aristotle categorizes the physical world, inventing biology and logic.
item.itunes:author: The Eternal Argument

item.title: Ep 6: Aristotle II: Virtue Ethics
item.description: The Nicomachean Ethics — How to live a good life in a polis.
item.itunes:author: The Eternal Argument

item.title: Ep 7: Epicurus & The Cynics
item.description: Pleasure vs. Dogs — Alexander the Great is dead; the world is massive and scary. Epicurus says "hide in the garden"; Diogenes says "bark at the emperor."
item.itunes:author: The Eternal Argument

item.title: Ep 8: The Stoics: Zeno, Epictetus, & Marcus Aurelius
item.description: Control & Duty — Roman Empire. From a slave (Epictetus) to an Emperor (Marcus), Stoicism becomes the operating system of Rome.
item.itunes:author: The Eternal Argument

item.title: Ep 9: The Skeptics: Pyrrho & Sextus Empiricus
item.description: Suspended Judgment — The clash of dogmatic schools. The Skeptics find peace by admitting they know nothing.
item.itunes:author: The Eternal Argument

item.title: Ep 10: Neoplatonism: Plotinus
item.description: The One & The Emanations — Late Antiquity (The decline of Rome). Philosophy turns mystical, preparing the ground for Monotheism.
item.itunes:author: The Eternal Argument

item.title: Ep 11: Augustine of Hippo: The Architect of the West
item.description: Faith, Time, and Sin — The Fall of Rome (410 AD). Augustine writes City of God to explain why the earthly empire failed and the heavenly one endures.
item.itunes:author: The Eternal Argument

item.title: Ep 12: The Islamic Golden Age: Avicenna & Averroes
item.description: The Aristotle Preservation Project — While Europe sleeps, Baghdad translates the Greeks. They reconcile the Quran with Aristotelian logic.
item.itunes:author: The Eternal Argument
